# SPARQL surface

Every function and keyword below was **probed against a running store** by
`crates/holos-engine/examples/surface.rs`, and the status column records what
actually happened. Where something is unsupported, the note is the engine's own
error rather than an editorial summary of it.

Regenerate with:

```sh
cargo run --release -p holos-engine --example surface > SPARQL-SURFACE.md
```

## How to read this

| | |
|---|---|
| yes | the probe evaluated and returned a result |
| no | the probe failed; the note carries the engine's own message |

A yes means *this build evaluates it*, not that every edge case of the specification is covered. The conformance suites in `README.md` are the measure of that: SPARQL 1.1 at 476/477 of what runs, SPARQL 1.2 at 262/266.


> **SPARQL Update** has its own keywords: `INSERT DATA`, `DELETE DATA`,
> `DELETE/INSERT ... WHERE`, `DELETE WHERE`, `LOAD`, `CLEAR`, `CREATE`, `DROP`,
> and `SILENT` on each. All are implemented, and all 94 W3C
> `UpdateEvaluationTest`s pass. They are not probed here because a probe would
> mutate the store the other probes read. See `OPERATIONS.md`.


> **Federation.** `SERVICE` evaluates against endpoints registered in-process.
> **Calling a remote endpoint over HTTP is deliberately not enabled**: a `SERVICE`
> IRI in a user's query would make the server issue a request to a host of the
> user's choosing, reaching cloud metadata at `169.254.169.254`, internal admin
> interfaces, and anything else routable from the server but not from the user.
> Remote `LOAD` is refused for the same reason. Enabling it needs an allow-list,
> which is a policy decision; see `ACCESS-CONTROL.md`.
>
> Results from another service have **not** passed through the policy chokepoint,
> so the guarantee in `ACCESS-CONTROL.md` covers the local contribution only.

#### Deliberately not implemented

| Function | Why |
|---|---|
| `fn:string-join` | takes a sequence; SPARQL has no sequence type |
| `fn:tokenize` | returns a sequence |
| `fn:distinct-values, fn:count, fn:sum` | sequence functions; use SPARQL aggregates |
| `fn:matches, fn:replace` | use SPARQL's REGEX and REPLACE, which are the same functions |
| `fn:doc, fn:collection` | retrieve external documents; that is the SSRF surface refused for LOAD and SERVICE |
| `fn:current-dateTime` | use SPARQL's NOW() |
| `afn:now` | use SPARQL's NOW() |
| `afn:bnode` | identity of a blank node is not addressable through this interface |
| `afn:sha1sum` | use SPARQL's SHA1 |
| `spif:cast` | use the xsd: constructor casts |
| `spif:parseDate, spif:dateFormat` | needs a format-pattern language; none is specified normatively |
| `spif:invoke, spif:eval` | evaluate a SPIN expression; there is no SPIN engine here |
| `spif:random` | use SPARQL's RAND() |
| `spif:regex, spif:replaceAll, spif:split` | use SPARQL's REGEX and REPLACE |

An unregistered function is **not** a parse error: it parses, and fails at
evaluation. Adding more is small, because they are ordinary
`fn(&[Term]) -> Option<Term>` entries on the evaluator, which is exactly how
`geof:buffer` and `geof:boundary` were added.

For `fn:`, the SPARQL built-ins cover the same ground under different names:
`UCASE` for `fn:upper-case`, `REPLACE` for `fn:replace`, `REGEX` for
`fn:matches`, `STRLEN` for `fn:string-length`.

## The complete GeoSPARQL set

45 functions: 43 from `spargeo`, plus `geof:buffer` and `geof:boundary`
implemented here. The table above samples them; the full list is:

area - asGeoJSON - **boundary** - **buffer** - centroid - convexHull - coordinateDimension - difference - dimension - distance - ehContains - ehCoveredBy - ehCovers - ehDisjoint - ehEquals - ehInside - ehMeet - ehOverlap - envelope - getSRID - intersection - isEmpty - isSimple - length - perimeter - rcc8dc - rcc8ec - rcc8eq - rcc8ntpp - rcc8ntppi - rcc8po - rcc8tpp - rcc8tppi - relate - sfContains - sfCrosses - sfDisjoint - sfEquals - sfIntersects - sfOverlaps - sfTouches - sfWithin - spatialDimension - symDifference - union

Names in **bold** are the two added by HOLOS.
